scenes.headline: How a quant release proves its files and drafts faster
scenes.sub: A signed manifest, and a draft head cut to 32,768 tokens
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Popcorn! This community quant of a Qwen model ships two things most don't: a signed manifest, and a trimmed draft head. Here's how both work.

scenes.label: What's new here
scenes.text: Trust you can check: a signed manifest lists every file's hash, and a public key in the same repo proves nobody changed it.
scenes.say: The idea is trust you can check. A signed manifest lists every file's hash, and a public key in the same repo proves nobody changed it.

steps.say: The release manifest lists every file with its exact byte count and hash.
A signature covers it, checked against a public key shipped in the same repo. Both signatures verify, and the key's own fingerprint matches.
The model files are too big to re-hash, so compare with Hugging Face's own file metadata instead. All twelve match.

items.say: The dense model already carries its own multi-token prediction head, which drafts tokens over the full vocabulary.
FastMTP is a second, trimmed copy of that head. Its output covers thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-eight tokens, so each draft step is cheaper.
A small patch scatters those scores back through a draft-to-target map, and every other token gets minus infinity.
The full model still verifies every drafted token, so the output can't change. Only the speed can.

scenes.label: document throughput with FastMTP at depth 3, against MTP disabled
scenes.note: self-reported, one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell; not reproduced here
scenes.say: HauhauCS reports up to three point zero two times the document throughput of no drafting at all, on one GPU. That's self-reported, and not reproduced.

scenes.text: A signed manifest makes a release checkable, and checking it costs nothing but bandwidth and a public key.

recap: A signed manifest hashes every file
FastMTP trims the draft vocabulary to 32,768
The target model still verifies every draft
scenes.say: To recap: a signed manifest you can verify, a trimmed draft head, and a target model that checks every draft.
